1.text: A tumour is not one enemy but a population of competing clones, each with its own mutations and its own fitness f_i. A clone gains share only when it beats the average: dx_i/dt = x_i(f_i − Σx_j f_j). Every treatment changes the fitness - and so it selects whichever clones it happens not to kill.

2.text: That is how $(thing)drug resistance$() arises: a resistant cell one in a thousand, with an advantage of s = 0.5 per day under treatment, is 96% of the tumour twenty days later. It was there before the drug - the drug chose it due to the natural selection process. Hence combination therapy: a clone resistant to two independent drugs at once is rarer by the product of their odds.

1.text: Between hosts, an infection is a bookkeeping process. Split a population into susceptible S, infected I and recovered: dI/dt = βSI/N − (γ + μ)I. At the start everyone is susceptible, and the infection grows only if each case makes more than one more: $(thing)R₀ = β/(γ + μ) > 1$(). Once a fraction 1 − 1/R₀ is immune, it can no longer spread.

The body destroys anomalous cells all the time. A tumour exists because it escaped detection. $(thing)Immune evasion$(): it sheds the markers T cells look for, shows PD-L1 to switch them off, and recruits cells that suppress inflammation. $(thing)Immortality$(): every division shortens the telomeres at the chromosome ends until a cell must stop - unless it switches $(thing)telomerase$() back on.

2.text: $(thing)Angiogenesis$(): beyond a millimetre it starves of oxygen, so it calls in new blood vessels (VEGF). Even then it slows: a tumour grows as N = K·exp(ln(N₀/K)e^{−αt}), fast when small and levelling off at the capacity of its supply. $(thing)Metastasis$(): cancer cells loosen their grip (the epithelial-mesenchymal transition), enter the bloodstream, survive the journey and grow again elsewhere. Most die; but it only takes one to recreate another tumour.

4.text: Telomerase switched back on: the chromosome ends rebuild themselves, and the cells forget how to grow old. They have outlived their donor.$(br2)Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().

Every science keeps a drawer of things that should not happen. Physics has defects and law violations through Black Holes, chemistry has molecules that self-propagates in the form of prions, biology has cancer, mathematics has indivisible numbers. $(thing)Abnormality & Infection$() studies them together, because they behave alike: they $(thing)arise$() from a broken rule, $(thing)replicate$(), $(thing)escape$() what should destroy them, and $(thing)change$() the normal world they live in.

This machine flips it locally and catches what falls out.
